items.title: Automating routine work
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: Automation uses software to do repeated tasks so people can spend time on work that needs judgement. Start by listing tasks you do weekly, note how long each takes and how often errors occur, and pick those that are frequent, simple and rule-based, such as sending reminders, copying data between systems or producing reports. Map the steps, build or set up the automation, and test it on a small scale before relying on it. Keep a person able to check it and to step in when something unusual happens. Measure the time saved. Do not automate a bad process; fix it first.

options.text: Letting software do repeated tasks so people can do work needing judgement

questions.prompt: What should you do before relying on an automation?

options.text: Test it on a small scale
Switch it on for everyone at once

questions.prompt: Why fix a bad process before automating it?

options.text: Automating a bad process only makes the problems faster
It saves no time either way

items.title: Closing accounts and deleting data
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: When a business closes, close its accounts and remove data in the right order. List every account: bank, payment providers, email, website and hosting, social media, software subscriptions, domain names and marketplace shops. Cancel in a way that stops payments, and keep copies of records you must retain, such as accounting and tax records, for the period required. Delete personal data you no longer need, or have no lawful reason to keep, from systems, devices and backups, and tell the people who hold it for you. Keep access until the work is done, then close it. Note what you did, with dates.

questions.prompt: What should you list before closing a business's online accounts?

options.text: Every account: bank, email, website, subscriptions and social media

questions.prompt: Which records should you keep when closing?

options.text: Those the law requires you to retain, such as accounting and tax records

questions.prompt: What should happen to personal data you no longer need?

options.text: It should be deleted, including from devices and backups

questions.prompt: Why note what you did, with dates?

options.text: It is evidence that you closed things properly
